head: 0feac0efb9c75c9e919a544b05306869eb99c691
summary:
The rework answers every finding from the first pass. The rule now covers the variable form Tag() uses, the P-004 fixture lists the case variant first, Get-Net uses an Ordinal dictionary, P-004 checks spellings against its own list, and PoolWatchCases gets Get-ScratchParent. The interrupt suffix is now worded from the marks that exist, the disposition table is in, the Q&A source is quoted in full, and the warm set starts after the first Completed F arm. Spike 107 settles the fork: on the FileRepository set, NtfF and the WC tags read exactly +0 on every warm repeat.

Two new majors. First, case 8 compares each unchanged fixture's -Report text with a 0feac0e copy, and that comparison cannot pass as written:
- C-011's output contains the PoolWatch.ps1 line number of the -Protocol throw and the boot age, both measured to differ by spike sc130.
- Some cases print the fixture's random run folder path.
- The 0feac0e copy of PoolWatchCases has no Get-ScratchParent, so under the engine's TEMP the baseline run hits lesson #391 itself.

Second, the spike-107 evidence step gives bare source paths for A-large and A-small. Those folders are not in the worktree; they sit under %APPDATA%\taad3\spikes\8\spike-107\. A builder following the text would write missing.txt for evidence that exists.

Six minors:
- The engine has already added the renamed rule as a second entry. The design's "single entry" instruction does not say which entry survives, and the four new patterns alone miss Read-Mark's `$WatchedTags -contains $_[0]` form.
- The guard branch drops HEAD's tags and system120089 checks on /before and /exit.
- The reading rule's "same-length idle movement" has no defined value for spans longer than the 1,200 s idle windows.
- The claim that lesson #349's +5-per-walk WC leak sits above the Sandbox's own idle movement of 2-9 is wrong arithmetic; it depends on how much the leak tags move at idle on the host.
- The 17-row disposition check can be satisfied with a duplicated row.
- Moving C-052's planted folders to Get-ScratchParent, while PoolWatch.ps1 -Rehearse still cleans up under GetTempPath(), breaks C-052 under the engine's TEMP.

findings.claim:
Cases 3, 7 and 8 compare -Report text with 'the same case run on a git worktree of 0feac0e'. As specified, that comparison cannot pass, and running the baseline is unsafe:
(a) C-011's output carries the PoolWatch.ps1 source line of the -Protocol throw and the boot age. Spike sc130 measured both changing between unfixed and fixed copies ('PoolWatch.ps1:691 vs :701', '78273 vs 78306 s'). Every edit this slice makes above -Protocol moves that line, so 'equals' fails on C-011 under pwsh 7 too.
(b) Several cases echo the fixture's run folder in -Report lines, for example C-055's 'ENVIRONMENT not readable: <dir>\prepare\prepare.json ...'. That folder holds a random case-<12 hex> name, and with Get-ScratchParent its parent changes as well.
(c) The 0feac0e copy of PoolWatchCases.ps1 has no Get-ScratchParent. Run under the engine's TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, the baseline is exactly the lesson #391 failure this slice fixes: red, or folders only an administrator can list.
(d) `git worktree add` writes a sibling directory and shared .git metadata. The spikes used `git archive` into scratch instead.
findings.evidence: Spike sc130-guard-stop-survives-interrupt-fix's evidence: the diffs were taken 'after replacing the random case-<12 hex> folder names', and C-011 differs in tree path, boot age and the trace line. PoolWatch.ps1:568 puts the run folder into the -Report line. PoolWatchCases.ps1:99 at 0feac0e roots fixtures in GetTempPath().
findings.fix: Build the baseline with `git archive 0feac0e tests/window` into a folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. Run both trees through one committed wrapper that sets TEMP=TMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and prints 'scratch:'. Compare only after normalising `case-[0-9a-f]{12}`, the scratch parent, `PoolWatch.ps1:\d+` and boot-age seconds, or leave C-011 out of the text comparison and keep only its exit code and its ok/FAIL counts.

findings.claim: The 'Spike-107 evidence, committed' component gives the A-large and A-small sources only as `run-20261012-002418\out` and `run-20261012-015214\out`. It marks only the FileRepository run as 'outside the worktree', which implies the other two are inside it. They are not: the worktree's .taad-scratch has no run-20261012-* folder. Both sit in separate spike folders under the engine's AppData. A builder following the text would conclude 'already gone' and write missing.txt for two of the three evidence sets behind the 'expensive' O-017 decision. That is the loss the component exists to prevent (spike 87's marks.jsonl and events.log).
findings.evidence:
Glob of .taad-scratch/**/run-20261012-* in the worktree returns nothing. The two folders do exist:
- C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Roaming\taad3\spikes\8\spike-107\sandbox-above-cap-warm-probe-repeat-ntff\.taad-scratch\sandbox\run-20261012-002418\out (analysis.txt, arms.jsonl, marks.jsonl, log.txt, ...)
- C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Roaming\taad3\spikes\8\spike-107\sandbox-below-cap-warm-probe-repeat-ntff\.taad-scratch\sandbox\run-20261012-015214\out\analysis.txt
Each spike folder also holds an earlier run (001824; FileRepository 005850), so the run ids matter.
findings.fix: Give full source paths for all three sets: the two above, plus the FileRepository run-20261012-011147 path. Allow missing.txt only after a Glob of %APPDATA%\taad3\spikes\8\spike-107\**\<run id> also finds nothing.

findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1172-1184 holds 'PoolWatch never compares pool tag names without regard to case', and :1186-1198 holds 'PoolWatch compares pool tags case-exactly'. Each has its own '# settled by SL-099' marker. A case-insensitive grep of the four new patterns over PoolWatch.ps1 finds 0 hits on HEAD, which is right.
findings.fix: Either keep both entries, which do not overlap and both report 0 hits on HEAD, and drop the 'single entry' instruction; or move attempt 1's `\$(WatchedTags|NetTags)\s+-i?(contains|...)` pattern into the new entry before deleting the old one. Either way, add `$WatchedTags -contains $_[0]` to the must-fire corpus.

findings.claim: The reworked guard branch checks only pagedBytes and nonpagedBytes on /before and /exit, and folds a miss into '(no <mark> mark | <mark> <field> is null)'. HEAD (:466-472) and attempt 1 checked all four fields on every mark, each on its own line. A guard-stopped arm whose /exit has tags null (Read-Mark's catch at :209) or system120089 null (:211) is then no longer named as incomplete. Review m7's contract for marks with missing parts is lost for exactly the arms whose net at the stop is their only figure.
findings.evidence: The guard-branch component reads: 'needs /before and /exit with non-null pagedBytes and nonpagedBytes'. Only non-interrupted arms keep HEAD's checks, and only on /settled. PoolWatch.ps1:199-200 and :209-211.
findings.fix: Keep HEAD's four-field checks on /before and /exit as separate MISSING lines, for interrupted and non-interrupted guard arms alike. Only the net clause needs pagedBytes and nonpagedBytes.

findings.claim:
Record item (d) bounds each tag by 'the largest same-length |movement| over I0/I1'. I0 and I1 are 1,200 s. Two of the spans the rule judges can be longer:
- the accumulation span, from the first warm arm's /settled to the last's, covers two or three arms of scan plus 600 s settle each, roughly 1,500-2,600 s;
- a cold F1 from /before to /settled can run to about 1,900 s (SL-044's 1,299 s C: scan plus 600 s).
No same-length idle window exists for those. Spike 107 hit the same gap and quietly substituted ('[no idle pair w=600 apart; used w=300]'). The rule is fixed before session 1 because changing it later costs a Restart, so it should say what to use. Two related gaps:
- If F1 is guard-stopped, '10% of F1's rise' should be the cold rise through the first Completed arm.
- Only Completed warm arms carry a /settled that can be judged.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:51 (WindowSec = 1200) and :53 (SettleSec = 600). Spike 107 A-large analysis.txt, criterion lines (2) and (3).

quote.text: WindowSec          = 1200    # I0 and I1, 20 min each

findings.claim: Cross-domain invariant 4 is marked 'holds' on the ground that 'Lesson #349's +5 WC per walk stays above an idle movement of 2-9'. +5 is not above an idle movement of 6-9. Spike 107's own A-large WC idle movements at w=120 were 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 2 and 6. So whether the host session can see a +5-per-walk WC leak depends on the leak tags' idle movement on the host during session 1. The only host figure is SL-095's scratch harness, which saw 0 over 2 minutes on a different boot. This is must-verify, not holds. (The FileRepository warm repeats read exactly +0, so spike 107 itself is not in question.)
findings.evidence: Spike 107 A-large analysis.txt, criterion (4): 'WCsc ... P2: d=+1 (idle 8)', 'WCse ... (idle 9)', 'WCfn ... (idle 2)', 'FMwi ... (idle 6)'. The FileRepository analysis.txt reads WCsc warm d=+0 against idle 5.
findings.fix: Mark invariant 4 must-verify. Record item (d) should say the WC reading can see a +5-per-walk leak only if the host's idle movement on those tags is under 5, and the person's reading should report that idle figure next to each WC verdict.

findings.claim: The disposition-table check passes when Select-String 'returns 17 rows'. A row duplicated for one id makes up for an id with no row, so the check still passes with a hand-off item dropped.
findings.evidence: The key_interactions of the 'Outcome-C redesign record' component.
findings.fix: Assert that the set of distinct ids captured by the pattern's first group equals the 17 named, and that no id appears twice.

findings.claim: The design moves :336 to Get-ScratchParent. :336 is where C-052 plants its 'rehearse-stale' and 'rehearse-live' folders. The rehearsal they test, PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol -Rehearse, still sweeps and roots its scratch in GetTempPath()\fsa-poolwatch (:654-655). Whenever TEMP is under the Windows folder, which is the case the change exists for, the planted stale folder sits in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-poolwatch while the sweep runs in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\fsa-poolwatch. The check 'a rehearse-* folder last written two hours ago ... is swept' then goes red, and the 'left alone' check passes trivially. This slice does not run C-052, but the measurement-preparation slice's guard-trip rehearsal will.
findings.evidence: PoolWatchCases.ps1:336-349 (plants and checks) and PoolWatch.ps1:654-655 (sweep and scratch root).
findings.fix: Either leave :336 on GetTempPath(), since C-052 is outside this slice's scope, or route PoolWatch.ps1:654-655 through the same Get-ScratchParent so both ends agree.

dimensions_checked.result:
Two findings:
- N2: the A-large and A-small sources are not where the paths imply; both were found under %APPDATA%\taad3\spikes\8\spike-107.
- N6: invariant 4's '+5 stays above idle 2-9' is wrong arithmetic; it depends on the host's leak-tag idle movement.
Checked and confirmed in spike 107's own analysis.txt files: NtfF +401 cold then +0/+0/+0 warm on A-large; FileRepository WC +961 cold then +0 warm; accumulation +4 and +5.

N8: moving :336 without moving PoolWatch.ps1:654-655 splits C-052's plant from the rehearsal's sweep under the engine's TEMP. The guardAtStart exclusion, the three-way suffix and the /settled checks for non-interrupted arms answer the previous m3 and the cascade case.

None new. The Get-Net Ordinal dictionary and the variant-first fixture make the case-exact invariant hold where it decides, answering M2 and M3. The P-004 text omits M4's always-live assertion, but that is owed to build under M4's accepted-pending disposition, so it is not re-filed.
None. The scope is the SC-130 fix, tag recording, guards, the record and the evidence copy. There is no judge, tolerance, purge or new arm type, and over_engineering_flag is honoured.

N5: the reading rule's 'same-length idle movement' has no value for spans over the 1,200 s windows; the cold rise after a guard-stopped F1, and which warm arms count, are not stated. The guard-line contract and the Get-Net contract are otherwise specified.

N4: the guard branch no longer names a null tags or system120089 on /before or /exit, a part Windows will not give (:199-211). The interrupt-before-/exit and throw-after-/settled paths are now worded correctly.

None. Q-178, Q-183, Q-184, Q-185 and Q-186 are respected, and session logs stay in SL-095-runs. Y3 is carried with SC-129's condition resolved. Every previous disposition is reflected in the design, with M4's always-live half owed to build.

N3: the engine has already appended the renamed rule as a second entry (.taad/fitness.yaml:1186-1198) beside attempt 1's. The 'single entry' instruction is ambiguous, and the four new patterns alone miss `$WatchedTags -contains $_[0]`. A grep of the four new patterns over HEAD's PoolWatch.ps1 finds 0 hits, as the design requires. The new strings are verdict-free.

N1: the baseline comparison against 0feac0e fails by construction on C-011's trace line and boot age and on fixture paths, and the baseline copy hits lesson #391 under the engine's TEMP. N7: the 17-row count check passes with a duplicated row. The P-003 arms (b)-(e), the P-004 halves and the :242 mutation otherwise cover the new branches.
None. Nothing is elevated. The new writes go under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and docs/design/SL-099-runs. The live read is an unelevated SystemPoolTagInformation query, as today.
